rounds.text: Loyal Equipments Ltd presents a compelling case for under-appreciation, underpinned by a significant margin of safety of 37.2% derived from a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 255 per share against the current market price of Rs 160 [E45, E46]. Long-term fundamentals demonstrate robust wealth creation, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 22% over 10 years and 25% over 5 years alongside a 10-year compounded profit growth of 29% and a 5-year profit growth of 50% [E14, E15, E18, E19]. Furthermore, historical return metrics remain healthy with a 10-year median return on equity of 16% and a 3-year median return on equity touching 20%, complemented by a solid current ROCE of 15.6% [E12, E26, E28]. Growth potential is actively supported by capital deployment, as evidenced by Capital Work in Progress surging by 484.6% to Rs 15.9 Cr in March 2026, signaling a major capex build-up phase [E41]. Additionally, a reverse DCF highlights that the market price currently implies a modest 11.6% earnings growth, which is well below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E47]. Domestic institutions have also initiated a stake increase to 0.52% as of June 2026 [E43]. Conceded: the stock price has suffered a severe 52% 1-year decline, sitting near its 52-week low with weak short-term profit growth and negative free cash flow [E21, E25, E36, E48].

The business suffers from severe operational inefficiency and profitability deterioration, highlighted by a negative ROE of -14.8% and a negative ROA of -5.69%, both lagging far behind sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Profit growth has stalled drastically, with compounded profit growth over the last 3 years dropping to 4% and trailing twelve-month profit growth plunging by -37% [E20, E21], accompanied by a net profit drop of -28% year-over-year [E64]. Cash generation is deeply alarming, evidenced by a dismal cash conversion ratio of 0.22x for Mar 2026 where operating cash flow accounts for only 28% of operating profit [E34, E37], culminating in a massive free cash flow burn of Rs -17.77 Cr [E36]. Leverage is climbing rapidly as borrowings nearly doubled to Rs 17.72 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 9.58 Cr a year prior [E40], while capital expenditures surge with CWIP up 484.6% to Rs 15.9 Cr [E41], increasing execution and financial risk. Market sentiment matches these fundamental cracks, as the stock languishes near its 52-week low at just 1% of its range [E48], trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50] with a relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500 [E51]. Conceded: long-term sales and profit growth over 5 and 10-year horizons show historical strength [E14, E15, E18, E19], and a discounted cash flow model suggests potential undervaluation with an intrinsic value of Rs 255 [E45].

Conceded: [E8], [E9], [E21], [E36], [E40], [E48], [E50], and [E51]. Despite these admitted pressures, the market's severe reaction ignores robust long-term compounding, featuring 10-year and 5-year sales growth of 22% and 25% respectively, alongside 50% 5-year profit growth [E14, E15, E19]. The fundamental strength vastly outpaces recent share price declines, a classic fundamentals-led dislocation where 5-year profit growth of 50% dwarfs 34% stock appreciation [E56]. Furthermore, the massive surge in Capital Work in Progress by 484.6% to Rs 15.9 Cr proves that the company is actively deploying capital into a major growth and capacity-building phase rather than suffering structural decline [E41]. This deliberate expansion justifies short-term cash burn and rising borrowings of Rs 17.72 Cr [E40], supported by a moderate overall debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.31x [E38]. Institutional confidence is actively building with domestic institutions increasing their stake to 0.52% [E43], while a disciplined reverse DCF reveals the current price only demands an 11.6% growth rate compared to the 18.0% base case assumption [E47].

Conceded: [E43]. The bull's narrative of robust long-term compounding overlooks severe short-term deterioration, highlighted by trailing twelve-month profit growth plunging to -37% and 3-year profit growth slowing to just 4% [E20, E21]. The touted 5-year profit growth of 50% [E19] clashes with a weak rules-based screen score of only 44 out of 100, which specifically flags a net profit drop of -28% year-over-year [E59, E64]. Furthermore, the massive 484.6% surge in capital work in progress to Rs 15.9 Cr [E41] has not fuelled immediate returns but instead triggered a staggering negative free cash flow of Rs -17.77 Cr and a ballooning of borrowings from Rs 9.58 Cr to Rs 17.72 Cr [E36, E40]. While debt-to-equity is moderate at 0.31x [E38], cash conversion sits at an alarming 0.22x with operating cash flow representing a mere 28% of operating profit [E34, E37], indicating that reported profits are entirely divorced from actual cash generation. Finally, the claim of a fundamentals-led dislocation [E56] ignores that the stock's relative-strength rating of 0 against the Nifty 500 and its position below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages reflect persistent, heavy market rejection rather than a temporary misunderstanding [E50, E51].
